headline: Advance Coastal Lodging and Marine Excursions
reservation: Standard hotel and vacation rental bookings are necessary, with a 4–6 month lead time suggested for summer oceanfront stays. Campsites at First Landing State Park fill rapidly for holiday weekends. Whale watching and boat tours require separate tickets through private operators; check official park pages for seasonal tram or tour schedules.

days.title: Resort Core and Coastal History

stops.name: Virginia Beach Boardwalk
stops.detail: Stroll or cycle the three-mile concrete path, passing the 24-foot bronze King Neptune statue.

stops.name: Cape Henry Lighthouse
stops.detail: Climb the 1792 structure for views of the Chesapeake Bay mouth; located on the Fort Story military base.

days.driving: Allow 30–40 minutes for local transit; summer traffic on Atlantic Avenue can be heavy.
days.note: Cape Henry Lighthouse requires valid ID for base entry; check military access status before visiting.

days.title: Swamps and Shorelines

stops.name: First Landing State Park
stops.detail: Hike the Bald Cypress Trail through prehistoric-looking wetlands draped in Spanish moss.

stops.name: Virginia Aquarium & Marine Science Center
stops.detail: View sharks and rays in glass tunnels and explore local marsh habitats featuring river otters.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; sights are clustered on the northern end of the city.
days.note: First Landing is the state's most-visited park; parking lots may reach capacity on summer weekends.

days.title: Wild Southern Reaches

stops.name: Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Observe migratory birds and wild pigs among the freshwater marshes and dunes.

stops.name: False Cape State Park
stops.detail: Access this remote beach only by foot, bike, or boat for a look at the untouched Virginia coast.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour to reach Sandbridge; transit into False Cape is non-vehicular.
days.note: Prepare for a long walk or bike ride as False Cape has no vehicle access for the general public.

intel.title: Oceanfront Metering
intel.text: City parking garages and meters are concentrated between 2nd and 40th streets. Rates and availability fluctuate significantly during summer festivals.

intel.title: Military Base Entry
intel.text: Access to the historic Cape Henry Lighthouse requires passing through a military security checkpoint. Check official Fort Story visitor requirements for current ID mandates.

intel.title: Southern Refuge Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable in the resort area but may drop in the remote marshes of Back Bay. Download trail maps for False Cape before heading south.

intel.title: Sandbridge Logistics
intel.text: Fuel stations are plentiful in the main city but sparse once you enter the Sandbridge residential area. Refill near Nimmo Parkway before heading to the refuges.

intel.title: Whale Migration Windows
intel.text: Humpback whale tours typically operate from December through February. Sightings are weather-dependent and boat capacities are limited.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Norfolk International Airport (ORF). Drive 18 miles east on I-264 to reach the oceanfront resort hotels for check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are ideal; RVs face strict parking restrictions in the resort area and narrow streets in Sandbridge.
plan.goldenHour: The Cape Henry Lighthouse area provides excellent low-light views of the bay, though sunset occurs over land, not the ocean.
